subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw make periodic memory sync a default-on fallback for missed watcher events, or keep `intervalMinutes` opt-in and solve this through docs/doctor/operator guidance?
rationale: The bug is real at source level, but the proposed fix changes default background sync behavior for existing users and root policy treats config/default fallback behavior as upgrade-sensitive.

options.title: Land a scoped default fallback
options.body: Accept a non-zero default periodic fallback after the linked PR is refreshed and proves upgrade behavior, interval dirty scoping, and docs/tests.

options.title: Keep interval sync opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at `0` and document or doctor-recommend `intervalMinutes` for users who need a watcher safety net.

options.title: Prefer watcher health recovery
options.body: Reject the default change and instead require explicit watcher liveness/error recovery that does not add default periodic indexing work.

recommendation.title: Land a scoped default fallback
recommendation.body: Accept a non-zero default periodic fallback after the linked PR is refreshed and proves upgrade behavior, interval dirty scoping, and docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent reviewer/merger of the adjacent memory watcher refactor is the best evidenced owner for deciding the watcher-default tradeoff or routing it to the right maintainer.
